key_insight: Human and LLM collaboration can accelerate materials synthesis by iteratively proposing and testing synthesis recipes, enabling discovery of a new structure type (Ba3PtO5) within a targeted homologous series.
engineering_relevance: This closed-loop human-AI workflow is a practical template for faster experimental planning in materials engineering, especially where synthesis pathways are complex and discovery is limited by trial-and-error.
method: Selected the Ruddlesden-Popper homologous series as a well-studied yet discovery-rich materials space.
Had humans and LLMs independently generate synthesis recipes for known and unknown targets.
Validated recipes in the lab and fed results back into subsequent rounds for closed-loop comparison.
evidence_signal: Across two rounds, humans and LLMs showed similar success on known materials but much lower success on unknown targets, and the campaign ultimately produced Ba3PtO5 as a new structural prototype.
watch_item: Performance on unknown materials was substantially lower than on known materials, so generalization to unfamiliar structure types remains uncertain and requires experimental verification.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
